text:
maria: Heads-up — production cluster 6 hit repeated OOM spikes this morning during a short KV-cache warmup. Not the usual big-batch case, looks like multiple small concurrent requests pushed workspace growth + kernel fallback churn.

aj: saw the alert. any profiling snapshots?

maria: yes attached excerpt from the live profile (trimmed):
```
PID 1421: peak_gpu_bytes=23.7GB
alloc_trace: workspace_alloc(8.2GB) -> kernel_select(slow_matmul_fp16->fp32_fallback) -> kv_cache_restore(4.6GB)
concurrent_streams=18, avg_seq_len=512, batching_win=30ms
```

ken: that kernel switch is expensive. If kernel selection flips to fp32 mid-request it blows up workspace. Could be our latency-based kernel selector misfiring when seq len spikes.

lina: we saw similar noise when the KV cache TTL was short and several hot prefixes rehydrated at once. That plus small batching windows meant more simultaneous allocations.

sre_oncall: mitigation ideas? can we triage live with a config toggle?

aj: propose a short playbook we can run immediately: 1) enable memory-hedging circuit (reduce max_concurrent_inflight from 20->12), 2) widen batching_win to 100ms for this model route, 3) temporarily raise KV cache TTL to 30m and enable aggressive prefix coalescing.

maria: +1. also add a transient buffer-reuse pass where we allow reuse across thread-local arenas (safe for deterministic workflows). That drops peak by ~10% in staging.

ken: how do we flip the circuit quickly? bruk deploy has a patch we can call:
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \\
  https://ctrlplane.internal/v1/routes/cluster6/patch \\
  -d '{"runtime": {"max_inflight": 12, "batching_win_ms": 100}}'
```

lina: TTL patch for kv cache:
```json
{"kv_cache": {"default_ttl_s": 1800, "prefix_coalesce": true}}
```
apply via `cfgctl apply cluster6-kv`

sre_oncall: I'll coordinate the flips and monitor memory graphs. Any automatic fallback we can enable if allocations keep climbing?

aj: yep — enable model-fallback policy to smaller quantized variant (q4_0) on OOM threshold 85% of GPU. Add 5s sticky window to avoid flip-flop. Config snippet: 
```json
{"fallbacks": {"oom_threshold_pct": 85, "fallback_model": "openlm/q4_0", "sticky_seconds": 5}}
```

maria: note: fallback will increase token latency a bit but keeps requests alive. Preferable to hard OOM. Also disable kernel auto-promote for this route while sticky window active.

ken: one more: enable request-shaping rule to reject very long sequences with a 413 + friendly user message when we detect current mem pressure. We have a compact handler: `reject_if_mem_pressure(seq_len > 1024)`

lina: implemented the TTL and batch window in staging, results: 12% lower peak, 18% fewer kernel switches in 10min run.

sre_oncall: rolling the config to prod now (started). I'm watching /metrics/gpu_mem and runtime logs.

dev-bot: Deployment started by sre_oncall at 2026-03-18T09:12:32Z — cfg change: max_inflight=12, batching_win_ms=100, kv_ttl_s=1800

maria: after the flip, two small incidents where fallback triggered for ~30s then cleared. avg latency +40ms for those requests. No OOMs recorded.

aj: solid. next actions before we revert: 1) create a lightweight rollout test that simulates concurrent rehydration (script in infra/tests), 2) add a permanent hedging flag into runtime so routes can opt in, 3) improve kernel selector to prefer stable kernels when workspace delta > 2GB.

ken: I'll file a perf ticket with profiling traces and suggested selector heuristic: "prefer stable path when predicted_alloc_delta > 2GB". assign to eng-runtime/allocator.

lina: and I'll add a regression alert: if kernel_switch_rate > 3/min and gpu_mem_free < 15% raise P1.

sre_oncall: good. leave this thread open until autoscaling + hedging rollout is validated for 24h.

maria: thanks all — saved prod from cascading OOMs. I'll drop the staging reproducible snippet in #eng-runtime later with the script. :thumbsup:
